_note: Photographs readers sent through the app, matched to a tree we map, waiting for a viewing pass. Judge with the photo-judge agent and apply with scripts/sightings_publish.py. Rebuilt on every knock from the rows without a verdict.

queue.recognise: A downy oak whose short, massive trunk splits low into five or six stems under one dense dome of a crown, in front of a pair of yellow gateposts with iron gates.
queue.story:
"The tree named 'Bella' is perfectly harmonious and reminiscent of the fractals," wrote the reader who sent us this oak from Ceciliano, in the hills just outside Arezzo.

Stand in front of it and you see what they mean. A short, massive trunk splits low into five or six stems, each dividing again and again into smaller limbs, until the crown closes into one dense green dome, the same branching repeated at every scale. Behind it stand the yellow gateposts and iron gates of a country house.

Italy counts it among its monumental trees. The national register lists this roverella, the downy oak Quercus pubescens, at Ceciliano, with a trunk 570 centimetres round and a height of 24 metres. In summe
queue.name: Bella di Ceciliano
queue.worth: the tree already has one: ship this only if it is better
